[reviewer-agent] Blocking:
- The branch diff contains only [module-di.test.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/packages/cli/src/lib/generators/__tests__/module-di.test.ts:1). There is no new Playwright test under any `__integration__` directory or `.ai/qa/tests`, so the task’s required integration coverage was not added. That conflicts with the QA guidance that executable Playwright tests are the expected artifact for integration coverage in this repo ([.ai/qa/AGENTS.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/.ai/qa/AGENTS.md:105), [.ai/qa/AGENTS.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/.ai/qa/AGENTS.md:205), [.ai/skills/integration-tests/SKILL.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/.ai/skills/integration-tests/SKILL.md:8), [.ai/skills/integration-tests/SKILL.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/.ai/skills/integration-tests/SKILL.md:94)).
- The added test only exercises `generateModuleDi` through a mocked resolver and temp filesystem ([module-di.test.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/packages/cli/src/lib/generators/__tests__/module-di.test.ts:18)). For CLI behavior consumed by scaffolded/standalone apps, the integration-test skill explicitly calls for create-app parity coverage (`yarn test:create-app:integration`) rather than stopping at unit tests ([.ai/skills/integration-tests/SKILL.md](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/.ai/skills/integration-tests/SKILL.md:201)). This change adds no such end-to-end coverage, so the real `mercato generate` path remains unverified.

Scoped validation I ran: `yarn workspace @open-mercato/cli test -- module-di.test.ts` passed.
[implementer-agent] Updated: Branch fix/hackon/hck-0091-tests-add-low-level-coverage-for-module-di-ts was synchronized by the coordinator.

[reviewer-agent] Blocking:
- [legacy TC-UMES-021](</home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/packages/create-app/template/.ai/qa/tests/TC-UMES-021.spec.ts:137>) is a byte-for-byte duplicate of [module-local TC-UMES-021](</home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/packages/create-app/template/src/modules/example/__integration__/TC-UMES-021.spec.ts:137>). In a scaffolded app, integration discovery picks up both files, and `npx playwright test --config packages/create-app/template/.ai/qa/tests/playwright.config.ts --list` shows two separate `TC-UMES-021` executions. That means the standalone parity suite runs the same filesystem-mutating generator scenario twice. The QA guidance says new coverage should live in the module-local `__integration__` path; the extra legacy `.ai/qa/tests` copy should be removed unless there is a separate legacy-only reason to keep it.

Focused verification: `yarn --cwd packages/cli test --runInBand src/lib/generators/__tests__/module-di.test.ts` passed.

[reviewer-agent] Ready: No blocking findings in the `module-di` coverage changes.

The new low-level Jest suite in [module-di.test.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/packages/cli/src/lib/generators/__tests__/module-di.test.ts:55) covers the main generator behaviors I would expect for this bug class: app override precedence, relative imports for `@app` modules, non-TS convention discovery, and checksum no-op writes. The added Playwright coverage in [TC-UMES-021.spec.ts](/home/hacker/repo/open-mercato/.workspace/worktrees/open-mercato/HCK-0091/packages/create-app/template/src/modules/example/__integration__/TC-UMES-021.spec.ts:137) is in the preferred module-local location and exercises the standalone-facing generator behavior end to end.

Validation I checked: `yarn --cwd packages/cli test -- module-di.test.ts --runInBand` passed, and the existing template Playwright artifact at `packages/create-app/template/.ai/qa/test-results/results.json` shows `TC-UMES-021` passing. Residual risk is limited to full scaffolded-app parity, which I did not rerun locally via `yarn test:create-app:integration`.
